findings.quote: Urdu (~230 million), though Urdu and Indonesian trade the tenth spot depending on the source
findings.why: ~230M matches the older Ethnologue figure (about 231M, 2023 edition). Later editions report Urdu higher, and some place Indonesian 10th. The page labels all counts as rounded Ethnologue-based estimates and names the Urdu/Indonesian ambiguity (also at line 242), so it is not a false statement. If the post is meant to cite Ethnologue 2025, re-check this one figure. Advisory, not a fail.

findings.quote: primarily from Brazilian and Cape Verdean backgrounds
findings.why: This leaves out the long-established Portuguese (largely Azorean) communities, which are a major share of Portuguese speakers in southeastern Massachusetts, Rhode Island and California. Better wording: 'including Portuguese (Azorean), Brazilian and Cape Verdean communities'. It is a general demographic remark, not a claim about Taika. Advisory, not a fail.
